pr.title: Feature flag: rolling-updates

raw_findings.body: The same recreate-upgrade result now returns 3, while 4 is assigned to the new feature-disabled condition, so consumers using the command's numeric exit status can misclassify the result or fail their upgrade workflow.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Scripted callers relying on the command's established exit-code contract take the wrong upgrade path.
raw_findings.impact: The same recreate-upgrade result now returns 3, while 4 is assigned to the new feature-disabled condition, so consumers using the command's numeric exit status can misclassify the result or fail their upgrade workflow.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch repurposes the existing recreate result code to reserve 4 for the new feature-disabled result.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Preserve RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE as 4 and assign FEATURE_DISABLED a distinct unused code, or provide an explicit compatibility migration before changing the documented script-facing status.
raw_findings.title: Changing the recreate result code breaks existing automation
raw_findings.trigger: An existing script runs update-compatibility check against incompatible metadata after upgrading to this version and branches on the previously returned exit code 4.

raw_findings.body: The operator still selects its upgrade logic from the update strategy instead of failing on the missing feature, so users are told to make an unnecessary configuration change and cannot rely on the documented fail-fast behavior.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Documentation and runtime behavior disagree, causing incorrect deployment expectations and masking invalid configuration.
raw_findings.impact: The operator still selects its upgrade logic from the update strategy instead of failing on the missing feature, so users are told to make an unnecessary configuration change and cannot rely on the documented fail-fast behavior.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new caution extends the CLI feature requirement to operator reconciliation without adding corresponding operator-side enforcement.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Either add explicit operator validation for the rolling-updates feature when an update strategy is configured, or change the caution to describe only the update-compatibility CLI commands that actually enforce the feature.
raw_findings.title: Operator documentation claims a feature gate that the operator does not enforce
raw_findings.trigger: A Keycloak CR configures an update strategy such as Recreate but does not enable rolling-updates in its feature list.

raw_findings.body: update-compatibility check could run without rolling-updates even though the new feature contract requires it, and the test suite would not detect the regression.
raw_findings.failure_mode: One of the two newly gated command paths can regress independently without test feedback.
raw_findings.impact: update-compatibility check could run without rolling-updates even though the new feature contract requires it, and the test suite would not detect the regression.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch adds a separate feature gate to the check subcommand but only adds a disabled-feature test for the metadata subcommand.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a distribution test that invokes update-compatibility check without --features=rolling-updates and asserts the disabled-feature error and exit status.
raw_findings.title: The disabled-feature path for the check command is not covered
raw_findings.trigger: A regression removes or bypasses this guard in UpdateCompatibilityCheck while the metadata command's disabled-feature test continues to pass.

raw_findings.body: The script-facing FEATURE_DISABLED=4 contract can silently break without the distribution test failing.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Tests validate human-readable output while missing an externally consumed machine-readable result.
raw_findings.impact: The script-facing FEATURE_DISABLED=4 contract can silently break without the distribution test failing.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new exit-status behavior is implemented but the added test verifies only the error text.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Assert cliResult.exitCode() equals CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED for the disabled metadata case, and apply the same assertion to the disabled check case.
raw_findings.title: The new feature-disabled exit code is not asserted by tests
raw_findings.trigger: The disabled-feature path returns a different status, such as success or the recreate status, while retaining the same error message tested by testFeatureNotEnabled.

finding.title: Changing the recreate result code breaks existing automation
finding.trigger: An existing script runs update-compatibility check against incompatible metadata after upgrading to this version and branches on the previously returned exit code 4.
finding.verifier_reason: The patch introduces a new feature (FEATURE_DISABLED=4) and reassigns RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE from 4 to 3. However, there is no evidence in the repository context that exit code 4 was previously documented or used by external scripts. The update-compatibility command is marked as Preview and the RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE constant appears to be newly introduced in this same patch context. The claim of breaking existing automation is ungrounded - no prior contract for exit code 4 is shown.

finding.title: Operator documentation claims a feature gate that the operator does not enforce
finding.trigger: A Keycloak CR configures an update strategy such as Recreate but does not enable rolling-updates in its feature list.
finding.verifier_reason: The documentation states the Operator will fail if rolling-updates is not enabled, but the candidate claims the operator does not enforce this. However, examining UpgradeLogicFactory.java shows the operator selects upgrade logic based on UpdateSpec.findUpdateStrategy() without checking the rolling-updates feature. The documentation caution is about the CLI commands (update-compatibility), not the operator reconciliation. The doc says 'the {project_name} Operator will fail' but this appears to refer to the CLI commands used by operators, not the Kubernetes Operator itself. The claim conflates CLI behavior with Operator behavior without concrete evidence of a mismatch.

finding.title: The new feature-disabled exit code is not asserted by tests
finding.trigger: The disabled-feature path returns a different status, such as success or the recreate status, while retaining the same error message tested by testFeatureNotEnabled.
finding.verifier_reason: The patch adds picocli.exit(CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED) at line 48 in UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.java. The test testFeatureNotEnabled in UpdateCommandDistTest.java only asserts the error message text (line 49: cliResult.assertError) but does not verify the exit code. The test at line 75 shows assertEquals(0, result.exitCode()) is used elsewhere, confirming exit code assertions are possible but missing for the FEATURE_DISABLED case.
